messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 PAGER: High 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate (us-west-2). Spike started ~2026-03-15T14:03:00Z. Pager: @samir.

samir: I'm oncall — looking at logs now. attaching first traces.

samir: errors look like 503s originating from inference-runtime: kv-cache-miss -> stream fail. rolling back recent routing change?

maria: I saw a rollout to quantized-model-v3 around 14:00 UTC. @samir can you confirm traffic split?

samir: traffic was 100% -> v3 for a small canary. kube-traffic shows 60% to v3 in us-west-2.

liz: tagging customer-impact: quickchat, acme-inbox, noteflow. they reported elevated errors via support.

alex: re: immediate mitigation — can we flip traffic to v2 fallback or scale inference service? i'd prefer fallback first.

samir: starting immediate mitigation: 1) scale inference-usw2 to +3 replicas (kubectl scale deployment inference-usw2 --replicas=8) 2) shift routing 90% -> v2.

[samir pasted code]

```
# scale
kubectl -n prod scale deployment inference-usw2 --replicas=8
# routing change (api-gateway):
POST /admin/route/update {"service":"inference","region":"us-west-2","split":{"v2":0.9,"v3":0.1}}
```

maria: started routing change. rolling restart not required. applying rate-limit to /v1/generate for 60s to drain queues.

[some minutes pass]

samir: scale completed, routing change accepted by gateway. error rate dropping from ~18% -> ~2% in the last 5m.

liz: :white_check_mark: Confirmed lower errors from customer side (support tickets updated).

alex: great — keep v3 isolated for now. next step: reproduce locally and capture heap/kv-cache metrics.

maria: taking on investigation. hypothesis: quantized-model-v3 causes larger than expected KV cache footprint which leads to eviction storms under load -> transient request failures.

samir: recording incident timeline and creating postmortem doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/incidents/PM-2345 (will update).

maria: scheduling postmortem meeting. proposed: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC. cc @liz @alex @samir.

liz: I can do write up for customer impact section (what customers saw, timestamps, CS notes).

samir: handing off oncall to maria at 14:50 UTC. leaving notes in oncall-runbook.

finance-billing: @maria quick question — finance needs estimated customer impact for SLA credit calc. please provide: total customer-minutes of degraded service, list of paid customers affected, and whether errors caused complete request failures vs latency spike.

maria: summary for finance: approx 22 minutes of elevated 5xxs (14:03–14:25 UTC). ~12 paid customers affected (most had intermittent failures, 3 had near-complete failures: AcmeCorp, QuickChat Inc, NoteFlow Pro). attaching ticket ids: SUPPORT-987, SUPPORT-991, SUPPORT-995.

finance-billing: thanks — can you also confirm whether we proactively issued any customer notices or credits already? need that for the billing ledger.

maria: we sent incident notification to affected tenants at 14:40 UTC (support channel + dashboard notice). no credits issued yet. awaiting postmortem for final decision.

finance-billing: ok. please include the following in the postmortem so we can start SLA credit pipeline: 1) precise start/end times per customer 2) whether mitigation restored full service or partial 3) root cause classification (platform bug vs config vs third-party).

alex: creating action items now — will add owners and due dates in the postmortem doc.

Action items (quick list):
- Maria: deep root cause analysis + reproducer (due 2026-03-19) :eyes:
- Samir: add auto-fallback policy to routing to prevent full rollouts on canary failure (PR + test) (due 2026-03-22)
- Liz: customer communication summary and per-tenant timelines (due 2026-03-16)
- Alex: RFC for kv-cache telemetry improvement (metrics + alert thresholds) (due 2026-03-26)
- Finance-billing: prepare provisional SLA credit calc template once we have per-customer mins (ongoing)

maria: added preliminary root cause note: model v3 increased kv-cache footprint by ~2.4x under production tokens which caused evictions; eviction storms led to request paths tripping fallback which surfaced as 503s. investigating whether quantization parameters introduced unexpected memory layout changes.

finance-billing: thanks. once postmortem is published please ping us with the finalized per-tenant minutes and whether those tenants are on SLA plans. we'll kick off the credits ledger and notify sales if needed.

samir: posting final incident closure note in thread after postmortem.

liz: postmortem meeting confirmed for 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC — invite sent. agenda: timeline, root cause, customer impact, remediation plan, SLA/finance next steps.

finance-billing: during the meeting, we should agree on: 1) which tenants are eligible 2) credit calculation method (per-customer downtime minutes * SLA rate) 3) owner to approve ledger entries.

maria: noted. i'll bring per-tenant logs and traces.

alex: i'll demo a quick dashboard query to extract per-tenant error minutes.

[some followup at end of thread]

finance-billing: FYI — provisional estimate looks like ~1.2k customer-minutes across paid tenants. rough ballpark of $3,500 in potential credits if all eligible. will finalize after postmortem.

maria: thanks — adding that to the postmortem executive summary.

samir: closing the live incident — mitigation successful, root cause investigation in progress. follow-ups tracked in PM-2345. :white_check_mark:

maria: handing off any remaining ops questions to infra team. will update thread with final postmortem link when ready. :spiral_calendar:
